name: Chinese Folk Horror
summary: Chinese Folk Horror ( 中式民俗恐怖 ) is the Folk Horror sub-genre based around traditional Chinese folk beliefs, funeral and marriage customs, folklores, and regional taboos.
description: Chinese Folk Horror ( 中式民俗恐怖 ) is the Folk Horror sub-genre based around traditional Chinese folk beliefs, funeral and marriage customs, folklores, and regional taboos. With a long history, it gained wide visibility on platforms like Bilibili, Douyin, and Steam since the 2020s. Visually, it relies on dim rural spaces, ritual symbols, and decayed old objects. The genre centers on the blurry boundary between the living and the dead, ancestral ethics, and karmic retribution, creating psychological horror by subverting familiar cultural customs.
culturalContext: Well-known zhi-guai (志怪) literature from the Spring and Autumn Period through the Qing dynasty is a source of inspiration for modern Chinese folk horror. Some must-read works of the Republic of China era, such as Diary of a Madman by Lu Xun, employed horror as a metaphor for social realities, inspiring the critical perspective in modern Chinese folk horror. The 1980s marked the golden age of Jiangshi fiction. These productions blended the folk custom of corpse escort, Taoist talismans, feng shui and fortune-telling with comedy and action, and were not purely folk horror. Since the 1990s, Hong Kong and Taiwan have produced numerous well-known folk horror films with a mature artistic style.
